title: Schematic images of quasi-compact stack morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and $Y$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $f:\mathcal X\to Y$ be quasi-compact [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Use structure sheaves and direct images evaluated by $(f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})(T)=\Gamma(\mathcal X\times_YT,\mathcal O)$ on etale scheme charts $T\to Y$ [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. There exists a smallest closed subspace $W\hookrightarrow Y$ through which $f$ factors, called its scheme-theoretic image; a closed subspace is given on etale scheme charts by a quasi-coherent ideal and its quotient ring sheaf. Its ideal is $\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$, and $|W|$ is the closure of the image of $|\mathcal X|\to|Y|$. The factorization $q:\mathcal X\to W$ is schematically dominant: $\mathcal O_W\to q_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ is injective. Formation of $W$ commutes with flat base change of algebraic spaces; here flatness is tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism]. In particular the base-changed $q$ is schematically dominant after any etale base change of $W$.

proof.text: Fix an affine etale chart $V\to Y$. The stack $\mathcal X_V$ is algebraic and quasi-compact, so choose an affine smooth surjective atlas $a:U\to\mathcal X_V$. Sections of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_V}$ inject into $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$: if a compatible family is zero on $U$, pull back along any object $T\to\mathcal X_V$. The algebraic space $U\times_{\mathcal X_V}T\to T$ is smooth surjective and has sections after an etale covering $\{T_i\to T\}$. On each $T_i$ the given family is the pullback of its zero component on $U$; the sheaf condition on $T$ makes its component zero. This also works after any base change of the atlas. Consequently $\ker(\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to\Gamma(\mathcal X_V,\mathcal O))=\ker(\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U))$. No quasi-compactness of $a$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 0CMK (lemma-existence-plus-flat-base-change), affine W_i construction; Tag 0CMJ (lemma-cover-upstairs), scheme-test descent argument

proof.text: Write $J=\ker(\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U))$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)/J)$. The scheme-image kernel theorem identifies $Z$ with the scheme-theoretic image of $U\to V$; $U\to Z$ is schematically dominant by the scheme-image theorem. If $V'\to V$ is any flat morphism of affine schemes, the map $U\to Z$ is a morphism between affine schemes, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $Z'=Z\times_VV'\to Z$ is flat. Flat pullback of schematic density makes $U'=U\times_VV'\to Z'$ schematically dense. Thus $Z'$ is the scheme-theoretic image of $U'\to V'$: it is a closed factorization, and any competing ideal in $\mathcal O_{V'}$ that vanishes on $U'$ vanishes on $Z'$ by the displayed injectivity. Its ideal is $J\mathcal O_{V'}$. All uses of quasi-separatedness here concern affine scheme maps, not $f$.

source.place: Tag 0CMK, proof of (c), reduction to schemes; Morphisms Tag 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image) and Tag 01R8

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$ on $Y_{\rm et}$. For every affine etale $V'\to V$ the base change $U'\to\mathcal X_{V'}$ is a smooth surjective atlas. Step 1 identifies $\mathcal I(V')$ with the kernel for $U'\to V'$, and step 2 identifies this with $J\mathcal O_{V'}$. Thus $\mathcal I|_V=\widetilde J$ as ideal sheaves on $V_{\rm et}$. Affine etale scheme charts form a basis, so these descriptions show that $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent. Use the closed-subspace/ideal correspondence to construct $W=V(\mathcal I)\hookrightarrow Y$ with $\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal I\simeq i_*\mathcal O_W$. In particular $W\times_YV=Z$. The kernels agree intrinsically, so no choice of atlas enters $W$.

source.place: Tag 0CMK, proof of (a); spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 082Z (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image) and 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals)

proof.text: The map $U\to V$ factors through $Z=W\times_YV$. For an object $T\to\mathcal X_V$, the smooth surjection $U\times_{\mathcal X_V}T\to T$ has sections on an etale covering $T_i\to T$. Therefore $T_i\to Y$ factors through $W$. Equivalently the ideal pulled back from $\mathcal I$ is zero there; it is zero on $T$ by the sheaf condition, so the closed-subspace factorization criterion gives $T\to W$. An arbitrary object of $\mathcal X$ is etale-locally over a scheme chart $V$ of $Y$, so the same argument gives its factorization. Uniqueness holds because a closed subspace is a subfunctor. These factorizations respect arrows and give $q:\mathcal X\to W$. If $f$ factors through another closed subspace $D$ with ideal $\mathcal K$, then every section of $\mathcal K$ pulls back to zero on $\mathcal X$, hence $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal I$. The inclusion-reversing ideal correspondence gives $W\subseteq D$. This proves minimality without inferring a scheme factorization from point-set containment.

source.place: Tag 0CMJ (lemma-cover-upstairs), scheme tests; Tag 0CPU (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-existence), factorization descent; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MB

proof.text: The map $|U|\to|\mathcal X_V|$ is surjective, so the image of $U$ in $V$ is the image of $\mathcal X_V$ there. The scheme-image theorem gives $|Z|=\overline{\operatorname{im}(|U|\to|V|)}$. Since $f$ factors through the closed subspace $W$, its image closure is contained in $|W|$. Conversely, let $w\in|W|$ and choose a point $v\in Z=W\times_YV$ above $w$ in an affine etale chart. For any open neighbourhood $N$ of $w$ in $Y$, its inverse image in $V$ is an open neighbourhood of $v$, hence meets the image of $U$ by the displayed density. Its image in $Y$ is a point of $N$ in the image of $\mathcal X$. Thus $w$ belongs to that closure. The atlas topology and point-surjectivity used here are precisely those of the stack-point topology lemma (which also applies to spaces).

source.place: Tag 0CML (lemma-topology-scheme-theoretic-image), affine chart and density argument

proof.text: For a flat map $Y'\to Y$, compare closed subspaces on affine etale charts $V'\to Y'$ that map to affine etale charts $V\to Y$. Such charts cover after pulling back a chart cover of $Y$ and refining by affine etale schemes. The composite $V'\to V$ is flat. Keep the atlas $U\to\mathcal X_V$ from step 1; its pullback $U\times_VV'\to\mathcal X\times_YV'$ is smooth surjective. The section-detection argument of step 1 and affine flat-base-change calculation of step 2 identify the kernel defining the image on $V'$ with $J\mathcal O_{V'}$. The ideal of $W\times_YV'$ is the same extended ideal by the closed-subspace correspondence. Hence the image constructed for $\mathcal X\times_YY'\to Y'$ is $W\times_YY'$ on this covering, and thus globally, since the correspondence is bijective. Quasi-compactness needed to construct that image follows directly from the base-change definition of $f$ being quasi-compact. No flat base-change theorem for the entire sheaf $f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CMK (lemma-existence-plus-flat-base-change), proof of (b),(c), specialized to a space target

proof.text: The map $q$ is quasi-compact: for any quasi-compact stack $T\to W$, its base change is $\mathcal X\times_WT=\mathcal X\times_YT$, since $W\to Y$ is a monomorphism, and this is quasi-compact by the hypothesis on $f$. Apply the kernel construction and factorization already proved in steps 1--4 to $q$. Its kernel $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ is quasi-coherent and cuts out a closed subspace $W_0\hookrightarrow W$ through which $q$ factors. The composite $W_0\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed subspace (on affine charts it is the quotient by the inverse-image ideal). Minimality of $W$ forces $W_0=W$, so the ideal correspondence gives $\mathcal K=0$. This is the asserted injectivity $\mathcal O_W\to q_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$. Finally step 6, applied to $q$, shows its scheme-theoretic image remains the whole target after any flat base change, in particular after any etale base change of $W$. Applying this same zero-kernel argument to that base-changed map proves its schematic dominance.
